title: How many cubes are in the staircase stack?
description: A stack of identical cubes rises like a staircase in a corner. The board counts the cubes layer by layer from the top, adds the layers, and checks the bottom layer by its rows.
teaching_notes: One idea: count a stack layer by layer, and count the hidden cubes that a visible cube rests on. Watch for students who count only the cubes they can see.

source: Figure it Out (shadows and views, question 5)
video_script.why: The child counts the cubes of a stack by layers, including the hidden cubes under the visible ones.
video_script.substitution: Read the stack as a staircase, count each layer from the top, then add the layers.
video_script.anchor: a stack of identical cubes that rises like a staircase in a corner, four layers high
video_script.payoff_line: There are twenty cubes, if every hidden place under a visible cube is filled

final_answer.value: 20 cubes, if every hidden place under a visible cube is filled
final_answer.spoken: twenty cubes, if every hidden place under a visible cube is filled

hold_back: Answer: 20 cubes, if every hidden place under a visible cube is filled
never_show: a count of only the visible cubes marked as right
video_script.design: A staircase stack of cubes in the anchor band. Its layers lift off one by one from the top, each is counted, and the counts are added.
open_questions: The stack of the book question is a picture that is not in the extracted text, so the video reads it as a four layer staircase in a corner, as the worklist steps do. The total of twenty cubes holds only if every hidden place under a visible cube is filled.
